title: Characters and Character Constants
learningObjectives: Explain the central rules behind characters and character constants in C.
Identify the relevant types, declarations, operators or library facilities.
Trace a worked example and explain its result.
Recognize common mistakes, portability concerns and unsafe assumptions.
Apply the concept in a small program and test normal and boundary cases.

understand.concept: In C, a character constant such as 'A' has type int in the ordinary execution character set. A char object stores a small integer value and may be signed or unsigned depending on the implementation. Character encodings map character values to code units; do not assume every character from every writing system fits in one char.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding character representation helps avoid incorrect assumptions about text, byte counts and signedness. C strings are sequences of char values terminated by a null character, but multibyte encodings mean one visible character may occupy multiple bytes.
understand.analogy: Think of a type as a contract that describes what kind of value an object can hold and which operations make sense for it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only an introduction; C types also determine representation, conversions, alignment and constraints.

explain.narrative:
In C, a character constant such as 'A' has type int in the ordinary execution character set. A char object stores a small integer value and may be signed or unsigned depending on the implementation. Character encodings map character values to code units; do not assume every character from every writing system fits in one char.

Understanding character representation helps avoid incorrect assumptions about text, byte counts and signedness. C strings are sequences of char values terminated by a null character, but multibyte encodings mean one visible character may occupy multiple bytes.

When reviewing code, identify the declared types first, then trace conversions and the exact expression being evaluated. Compile with warnings enabled and test boundary values. Do not rely on assumptions about another compiler or machine.

practise.guidedTask: Write a program that stores a letter, a digit character and a newline character. Print them with %c and inspect their integer values where appropriate.
practise.independentTask: Read a line of UTF-8 text and explain why strlen counts bytes rather than user-perceived characters. Avoid assuming one char equals one Unicode character.
hints: A character constant such as 'A' has type int in C.
char may be signed or unsigned depending on the implementation.
Use %c for character output and %d for an integer value.
Escape sequences such as \\n and \\t represent special characters.
A UTF-8 character can occupy multiple bytes.
